verdict.rationale: Next.js documents server data loading by making components async and awaiting data, and it streams UI integrated with the App Router and React Suspense, which covers the responsive-loading-UI half of the story. Nothing in the evidence shows a resource primitive that exposes server-loaded data as reactive state that updates in place. missing for 10: a resource-style reactive state primitive for server data, documentation of how loading/refetch states are managed reactively, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the Suspense loading UX.

support.subject: As a developer, I can treat server-loaded data as reactive state and build a responsive loading UI for it using resource and suspense primitives

citations.quote: Instantly stream UI from the server, integrated with the App Router and React Suspense.
Make your React component async and await your data.
